Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap so we have alignment on SLOs and next steps for a dedicated-capacity validation: 

What I heard (please correct if I missed anything):
- Primary experience: interactive clinician-facing assistant (short multi-turn). Target p95 end-to-end latency: 350-450 ms.
- Secondary: background summarization/batch jobs (not latency-sensitive) — p95 OK up to ~2s.
- Concurrency/throughput: peak concurrent users around 50–70, average session payload ~60 tokens output, peak burst concurrency up to ~120 for short windows.
- Streaming: partial tokens displayed in the UI; target chunk latency <= 200–250 ms for a smooth typing experience.
- Security & compliance: SOC2 and VPC/private deployment required for the validation cluster.

Ask from our side: please share a representative traffic CSV (timestamps, request size, response token distribution). You mentioned you could share that after the call.

What we will provide:
- A recommended dedicated sizing plan (GPU type, reserved throughput, and burst policy) for your SLOs.
- A 2-week validation sandbox runbook and test harness so you can run your UI/traffic profile against a dedicated cluster.
- Expected performance numbers (p50/p95/p99) across candidate GPUs and a short runbook for streaming tuning (chunk size, flush interval).

Next steps proposed:
1) You share the traffic sample and confirm the exact model family you plan to run (you mentioned a ~13B model today).
2) We’ll send a short sizing recommendation and a proposed validation window (2 weeks) by Wednesday.
3) If the sizing looks good, Redwood provisions a dedicated sandbox (VPC) for your team to run the harness.

Attachments referenced: neroli_slo_matrix.xlsx (blank SLO sheet for you to fill) — I’ll attach it to this thread.

Thanks — talk soon.

Confirming details:
- Interactive UI target: p95 <= 400 ms (end-to-end). We can tolerate up to 500 ms in some flows but prefer under 400 ms.
- Background batch summarization: p95 <= 2s — lower priority.
- Concurrency: steady-state 40–55 concurrent active users, daily peak spikes to ~110 for short events (2–5 minutes).
- Typical reply size: median ~45 tokens, 95th percentile ~120 tokens.
- Streaming: we want token chunks to appear in the UI every 150–250 ms for perceived responsiveness.
- Model: we are planning to run a fine-tuned 13B open model (private weights) — latency will matter more than raw throughput.

Attached: neroli_traffic_sample.csv — two days of anonymized traffic (timestamps, request size, tokens_requested, ui_flow). Also attached a short doc with compliance checkpoints.

Hi Alice / Vanessa —

I pulled the traffic sample and sketched an initial dedicated sizing plan for the 13B family you mentioned. High-level guidance below (numbers are estimates for a mixed workload, will refine during the sandbox run):

Assumptions from the traffic sample:
- Median output = 45 tokens, p95 = 120 tokens.
- Steady concurrent active users = 50, peak burst concurrency = 110.
- Model: quantized 13B (int8/awq-style) with KV cache enabled for multi-turn sessions.

Performance/ GPU candidate comparisons (expected p95 end-to-end for a single-request short response):
- NVIDIA H100 (quantized, optimized kernels): p95 ≈ 100–160 ms
- NVIDIA A100 40GB (well-optimized): p95 ≈ 140–230 ms
- NVIDIA A10G / T4 (cost-optimized inference cards): p95 ≈ 240–420 ms (more variance under burst)

Throughput & reserved capacity guidance (targeting interactive p95 <= 400ms with headroom):
- Baseline reserved throughput: 60 RPS sustained (covers steady concurrency ~50 with average 45 tokens).
- Burst/Autoscale policy: headroom to 220 RPS for short windows (to handle the 110-user spike pattern).
- Recommendation: 2 x A100 40GB nodes as the minimum dedicated pool for validation. That configuration should comfortably hit p95 ≈ 150–220 ms in our internal runs and gives room for caching + batching. If you want single-GPU minimum, H100 single node would meet the most aggressive latency targets but has higher cost/availability considerations.

Streaming recommendations to meet chunk latency 150–250 ms:
- Emit partial tokens with a 120–200 ms flush interval in the runtime (smallest per-token emission without increasing kernel calls).
- Use prefix/KV caching for multi-turn sessions so subsequent turns avoid full generation overhead.
- Configure small continuous-batch windows (5–10 ms) for throughput smoothing but keep max batch size limited to keep p95 low.

Operational notes:
- We'll wire up token-level cost telemetry and per-route SLO dashboards in the Redwood Console during the sandbox so you can see p95/p99 and billing impact per test.
- Recommend enabling local response caching for deterministic prompts (FAQ flows) to reduce load.

Attachments: gpu_choice_summary.pdf — quick side-by-side cost/latency estimates and a one-page runbook for the 2-week validation.

If you confirm the validation window, I’ll coordinate with infra to provision the VPC sandbox with the 2x A100 pool and provide SSH/ingress details and the test harness link.
